review_notes: I read the whole file. It has one definition, `TauCeti.torusChartedSpace`. It gives `Circle × Circle` a `ChartedSpace` structure modelled on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`. The structure is built by composing Mathlib's product charted space over `ModelProd (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))` with a singleton chart from `EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd`. I searched Mathlib/Geometry for "torus" and for `finAddEquivProd` and found nothing. The only relevant Mathlib instance is `ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1)) Circle` in Sphere.lean (line 570). Mathlib's product structure on the torus uses the model `ModelProd`, not `ℝ²`. So the Euclidean-model chart is a different representation, not a competing duplicate. The file deliberately makes it a definition rather than an instance so both models can coexist. It is built from existing Mathlib pieces (`ChartedSpace.comp`, `singletonChartedSpace`) rather than a new concept. I found no justified finding.
